A repo search for `reset_round_state(` returns only the definition. That means `_realloc_depth` is never cleared, so once a task hits `max_realloc_depth`, later rounds inherit the stale depth and can be blocked permanently.

FOLLOW: This makes the reallocation guard actually obey its own round-boundary contract. It also turns `reset_round_state()` into live code, so any other state that is truly per-round must be reviewed under that method instead of remaining silently lifetime-scoped.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Call `self.failure_handler.reset_round_state()` once per completed round in `process_round()`.

FINDING_ID: IM_F003  
SEVERITY: 0.87  
FLAW_CLASS: 2  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.75  
DESCRIPTION: `process_round()` feeds the immune per-model monitor the wrong failure signal.  
FIND: At [`bench/dynamic_management.py:5481`](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L5481), `failed` is computed as `mid not in responses or not responses[mid].parseable`. But `FailureHandler.detect_failure()` has already classified richer failures at [`bench/dynamic_management.py:5370`](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L5370). That means EMPTY, TIMEOUT, and FORMAT failures with `parseable=True` are passed into `record_model_round()` as `failed=False`, so the immune layer misses repeated hard failures. An empty response is the clearest example: it returns `FailureType.EMPTY` at [`bench/dynamic_management.py:4527`](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L4527) but still counts as “not failed” under the current boolean.  
FIX:
```python
<<<<
            fc = _model_finding_counts.get(mid, 0)
            failed = mid not in responses or not responses[mid].parseable
            resp = responses.get(mid)
====
            fc = _model_finding_counts.get(mid, 0)
            resp = responses.get(mid)
            failure_type = failures.get(mid)
            failed = (
                mid not in responses
                or failure_type in {
                    FailureType.EMPTY,
                    FailureType.TIMEOUT,
                    FailureType.MALFORMED,
                    FailureType.FORMAT,

>>>>
```
FOLLOW: This will make `model_failure` pathology detection reflect actual transport/protocol failures rather than just parseability failures. It also means repeated EMPTY/TIMEOUT/FORMAT rounds can now trigger `model_failure` remediation, which is the intended downstream behavior of the immune layer.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Derive `failed` from the already-computed `FailureType`, not from `parseable` alone.

ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.69  
DESCRIPTION: `chain_exhaustion_rate` is mathematically damped by double-counting, so the self-diagnosis threshold is effectively unreachable.  
FIND: At [`bench/dynamic_management.py:3451`](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L3451), the rate is `len(recent_exhaustions) / (len(recent_outcomes) + len(recent_exhaustions))`. In the normal path, every exhaustion also produces a remediation outcome entry first at [`bench/dynamic_management.py:3338`](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L3338), so exhaustions are counted in both numerator and denominator. That bounds the rate at `<= 0.5` whenever exhaustions are a subset of outcomes, but `self_diagnose()` only triggers when `exhaust_rate > 0.5` at [`bench/dynamic_management.py:4245`](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L4245).  
FIX:
```python
<<<<
        recent_outcomes = self._remediation_outcomes[-10:]
        recent_exhaustions = self._chain_exhaustion_history[-5:]
        total = len(recent_outcomes) + len(recent_exhaustions)
        if total == 0:
            return 0.0
        return len(recent_exhaustions) / max(1, total)
====
        recent_outcomes = self._remediation_outcomes[-10:]
        recent_exhaustions = self._chain_exhaustion_history[-5:]

        encounter_keys = {
            (entry["pathology"], entry["round"])
            for entry in recent_outcomes
        }
        exhaustion_keys = {
            (entry["chain_key"], entry["round"])

>>>>
```
FOLLOW: After this fix, chain exhaustion can actually cross the `> 0.5` threshold and produce the intended CRITICAL self-diagnosis. Expect more human-defer recommendations on runs where chains are genuinely too short.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Compute exhaustion over unique recent encounters, not over `outcomes + exhaustions`.  
VERIFIED: TRUE
